# ojothemes

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-stable-brightgreen.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#stable)
[![pkgdown](https://img.shields.io/badge/pkgdown-site-blue.svg)](https://openjusticeok.github.io/ojothemes/)
<!-- badges: end -->

`ojothemes` contains [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) and [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com/) themes for the Oklahoma Policy Institute (OPI) and Together Oklahoma (TOK) house styles, along with tools for fonts and plot export that make graphics reproducible on every machine.

## Installation

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("openjusticeok/ojothemes")
```

## Fonts

Source Sans 3 ships inside the package (variable font, SIL OFL) and is registered with `systemfonts` at load time — no font installation, admin rights, or network access needed. Every theme defaults to it, so plots render **pixel-identically** on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Proprietary fonts (e.g., Adobe Myriad Pro) are supported through a `fonts/` drop-in folder in your project; see `ojo_fonts()` and the vignette.

## Example

```{r example}
library(ojothemes)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point() +
  ojo_labs(
    analyst_name = "Brancen Gregory",
    source = "oscn",
    title = "Oklahoma Policy Institute",
    subtitle = "House-style plotting with ojothemes",
    x = "Displacement",
    y = "Miles per gallon"
  ) +
  theme_opi()

p
```

Styled tables work the same way with `gt`:

```{r gt}
library(gt)
gt_opi(mpg[1:6, 1:6])
```

## Exporting

``` r
# Pass communications specs verbatim, in any unit
ojo_save_png(p, "plot.png", width = 1080, height = 675, unit = "px", dpi = 144)
ojo_save_svg(p, "plot.svg", width = 178, height = 127, unit = "mm")
```
